security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, fenced code examples, JavaScript template literals, and normal sample networking patterns. I found no prompt injection, malicious intent, credential exfiltration, or skill-executed commands in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Static scanners may misread Markdown backticks as shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Keep code examples fenced with explicit languages and avoid shell-like snippets unless they are required for the skill.

remediation.issue: The API client example sends bearer tokens to a configured backend URL.
remediation.suggestion: State that EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL must point only to the trusted application backend and should use HTTPS in production.

content.value_statement: Expo authentication often fails because OAuth redirects, token storage, and route guards must align across app and backend. This skill provides concrete React Native patterns for Google sign-in, secure token handling, protected routes, and backend token verification.
actual_capabilities: Shows Expo AuthSession setup for Google OAuth in React Native apps.
Recommends expo-secure-store for access and refresh token storage.
Outlines an AuthProvider and useAuth context pattern for session state.
Demonstrates Expo Router redirects for authenticated and unauthenticated routes.
Shows how to attach bearer tokens to backend API requests.
Includes FastAPI guidance for verifying Google ID tokens server-side.
limitations: It is guidance, not a complete authentication service or package.
Client IDs, redirect schemes, and backend endpoints must be supplied by each project.
Refresh token rotation and revocation are mentioned but not fully implemented.
It focuses on Expo and Google sign-in, not every identity provider.

use_cases.title: Add Google Sign-In to Expo
use_cases.description: Use the AuthSession pattern to configure client IDs, scopes, and redirect handling for an Expo app.

use_cases.title: Protect App Routes
use_cases.description: Apply the auth context and Expo Router examples to redirect users based on session state.

use_cases.title: Verify Tokens on the Backend
use_cases.description: Use the FastAPI reference to validate Google ID tokens with the correct web client ID.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design secure access token and refresh token storage for my Expo app using expo-secure-store.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Redirect Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to diagnose why my Expo Google sign-in opens the browser but does not return to the app.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Expo auth flow, protected routes, token refresh plan, and backend Google token verification approach.

output_examples.input: I need Google login in an Expo app.
output_examples.output: A setup plan covering AuthSession imports, maybeCompleteAuthSession placement, client IDs, scopes, and redirect URI checks.

output_examples.input: My app forgets the user after restart.
output_examples.output: A session persistence review focused on secure token storage, startup restoration, backend validation, and logout cleanup.

output_examples.input: Backend token validation fails for Google sign-in.
output_examples.output: A verification checklist covering web client IDs, Google token validation, returned user fields, and common client ID mistakes.

best_practices: Store tokens with expo-secure-store instead of AsyncStorage.
Validate saved tokens with the backend before restoring a session.
Keep OAuth client IDs and redirect schemes aligned across Expo and provider settings.
anti_patterns: Using the iOS client ID for backend Google token verification.
Trusting a stored token without checking it against the backend.
Testing only in Expo Go while ignoring standalone build redirect URIs.

faq.question: Does this skill install an authentication library?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns and examples for Expo and React Native authentication.

faq.question: Which providers are covered?
faq.answer: The examples focus on Google sign-in, with patterns that can guide other OAuth providers.

faq.question: Why does it recommend expo-secure-store?
faq.answer: expo-secure-store is designed for sensitive values and is safer for tokens than AsyncStorage.

faq.question: Does it include backend code?
faq.answer: It includes a FastAPI reference pattern for verifying Google ID tokens on the backend.

faq.question: Can it help debug redirect_uri_mismatch errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists redirect URI configuration checks for Google Cloud Console and Expo app schemes.

faq.question: Is it specific to Expo Router?
faq.answer: The protected route example uses Expo Router, but the auth context pattern is broadly useful in React Native.
